name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
archDisplay: 552B sparse MoE, 40-layer causal encoder-decoder (1 shared + 384 routed experts, 6 routed active per token), ~8B active in prefill / 16B in decode, ~890 bytes/token global KV cache (about 1/4 of V4-Flash); natively multimodal (image+text in, text out); ~45T multimodal pre-training tokens
note: DeepSeek's 2026-09-10 release, the smallest model of a new architecture family: a 552B-backbone causal encoder-decoder MoE that activates ~8B parameters in prefill and 16B in decode, with native image input, a 1M context and a KV cache about a quarter the size of V4-Flash's. Open weights under MIT. On DeepSeek's own table it beats every compared model on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (90.6), DeepSWE v1.1 (74.2), Codeforces (3471), CyberGym (88.1) and AutomationBench (54.8), but trails the closed frontier on HLE and Terminal-Bench 3.0/4.0. The API alias deepseek-flash pointed to it until 2026-10-17, when DeepSeek replaced it with the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 checkpoint at the same prices, and the legacy V4-Flash names now route to 1017 too. DeepSeek later reversed its plan to serve deepseek-v4-pro requests with V4.1-Flash after 2026-09-14; the API still lists DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 under that name.
